indicator_definition: This indicator measures the proportion of seats held by women in national parliaments (single or lower chamber), expressed as a percentage of all occupied seats. Data are provided by the Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU) and compiled by Eurostat.
rationale: Equal participation of women and men in political decision-making is a fundamental dimension of gender equality and democratic governance. Increasing women's representation in parliament ensures that women's perspectives and interests are reflected in legislation and policy. Progress means an increasing share of seats held by women.
methodology_characteristics: Data are provided by the Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU) and refer to the situation on 1 January of each year. The indicator covers single chambers and the lower chambers of bicameral parliaments. Figures refer to the percentage of women among all members of parliament with a valid mandate.
indicator_name: Seats held by women in national parliaments
